source.title: Post-Training Science for Supervised Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Charles O'Neill; M. Jayasekara; Harry B. Partridge

record.tranche_reason: The study reports SFT results about validation loss, task scores, IFEval, and Fisher-trace flatness, but does not measure the training–test error gap or test any listed version's stated outcome. Its flatness findings concern task quality and retained instruction-following, not the generalization gap.
record.gate_note: The study's own batch, optimizer, scaling, and regularization results concern SFT validation loss or downstream task performance, not the training–test gap in the claim. The Fisher-trace analyses measure a proposed flatness property, but relate it to judged task quality or IFEval rather than the gap. Cited prior-work results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The fixed-one-epoch batch sweep tests V5 in language-model supervised fine-tuning: smaller batches reach lower held-out NLL (§2.3). V5 concerns held-out performance and does not require measuring a training–test gap. The Fisher-trace results do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure or generalization-gap ranking.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase captures the main Fisher-trace conclusion but needs qualification: pooled within-recipe analyses provide no reliable additional ranking, while genuinely loss-matched pairs weakly favor flatter cells. Flatness tracks retained instruction-following most clearly across optimizers. The authors also conclude that smaller batches reach lower validation loss at a fixed one-epoch budget.
record.recipe_differences: SFT experiments on customer datasets and task evaluations; measured validation loss, Fisher trace, and downstream task scores rather than generalization gaps for the listed interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Fisher-trace association changes with the comparison: pooled base-model association largely reflects model size; within fixed model/dataset/recipe at matched loss it does not reliably rank in-domain quality; across epochs it relates in opposite directions to IFEval and in-domain score; across optimizers it tracks IFEval.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-model Fisher-trace associations with judged quality largely reflect scale. Fine-tuned pooled associations are inconsistent, although genuinely loss-matched pairs favor flatter cells in 57–77% of comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fisher trace has comparison-dependent associations with in-domain SFT quality.

fits_no_version.finding: Across epochs, higher Fisher trace accompanies lower IFEval but higher in-domain score at fixed loss; Muon checkpoints have lower trace and higher IFEval than AdamW checkpoints on all four datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fisher trace can track retained instruction-following across SFT epochs and optimizer changes.

record.problems: The downstream judge is the criterion the training data was generated to satisfy, so it is not independent of the training objective. The base-model correlations use only nine models and are strongly confounded by model size. Fine-tuned Fisher-trace probes use 64 samples; Muon task-judge comparison uses 200 rows and one checkpoint per arm. Four divergent docs cells were excluded from the fine-tuned in-domain analysis.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result directly measures the training–test error gap or another outcome specified by V1–V8; therefore no SFT batch, optimizer, size, epoch, or adapter result was entered as a row for those versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Widening beyond the zero-training-error threshold in networks trained to convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited and broader tuning; the study compares AdamW with hybrid Muon.
The workload-dependent critical batch size, batches beyond the tested 8–64 range, and whether longer training or adapted scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization removes the penalty.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, training–test error gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Add fixed-epoch batch-versus-validation-NLL comparisons by model, dataset, and tuner. The record incorrectly excludes these on the premise that V5 requires a training–test gap. The prose establishes the direction; numerical batch penalties need extraction from the frontiers.

record.verdict_notes: The record's generalization-gap requirement is too restrictive for V5. Its rows_left_out statement excludes batch results through this mistaken interpretation, so those results require repair. No existing row supports the V5 verdict; it rests on the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out generalization.
Width beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization gap under the stated tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization gap under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout's effect on held-out error in the stated regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: nine base models (six Qwen3 and three Llama)
rows.operation_detail: Measured Fisher trace and judged task scores on 200 canonical-test rows per dataset.

conditions.value: four customer evaluations: security, leasing, support, docs

rows.measure: Pooled association between per-parameter Fisher trace and judged task quality; pooled Spearman values are −0.90 to −0.95 by dataset, and size-adjusted partial is approximately −0.15.
rows.note: This is a base-model association with task scores, not a training–test error gap. The authors note the pooled association largely re-expresses model scale.
rows.check: Figure 17's per-dataset pooled correlations range from −0.87 to −0.95, not −0.90 to −0.95; −0.90 is the aggregate reported in the prose. These measure judged quality, not V7's generalization gap.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B, LoRA and FullFT
rows.operation_detail: Compared Fisher trace with judged in-domain task quality across learning-rate and batch cells.

conditions.value: 220 in-domain pairs after four divergent docs cells were excluded
within model, dataset, and tuner; matched-loss analyses

rows.measure: At matched loss, Fisher trace added no reliable ranking of judged quality; pooled Spearman correlations were −0.50, −0.41, −0.36, and +0.35 across the four model–tuner groups.
rows.baseline: Validation loss ranked judged quality within each recipe, with within-dataset-standardised Spearman −0.38 to −0.88.
rows.value: Fisher trace did not provide reliable matched-loss ranking.
rows.note: The outcome is judged task quality at matched loss, not the train–test gap. Four divergent docs cells were excluded after exceeding the judge-error gate.
rows.check: The four reported correlations are pooled trace–quality associations, not themselves loss-controlled estimates. Qualify the blanket matched-loss null: §4.3 reports that genuinely loss-matched pairs favor the flatter cell in 57–77% of comparisons. Neither analysis measures V7.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B FullFT
rows.operation_detail: Compared Fisher trace and IFEval strict accuracy across epoch-sweep checkpoints.

conditions.value: standardised within model, arm, and dataset
trace–IFEval partial Spearman at fixed loss

rows.measure: Higher trace tracked lower IFEval capability, partial ρs = −0.19 at fixed loss.
rows.note: The reported relationship is with general instruction-following, not training–test error.
rows.check: The −0.19 partial correlation is reported across the epoch sweep, standardized within model, arm, and dataset; its attribution exclusively to Qwen3-8B FullFT is unsupported. IFEval retention does not measure V7's generalization gap.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B FullFT
rows.operation_detail: Compared Fisher trace and in-domain task score across epoch-sweep checkpoints.

conditions.value: standardised within model, arm, and dataset
trace–task-score partial Spearman at fixed loss

rows.measure: Higher trace tracked higher in-domain task score, partial ρs = +0.34 at fixed loss.
rows.note: The reported relationship is with task score, not training–test error.
rows.check: The +0.34 partial correlation is reported across the epoch sweep, standardized within model, arm, and dataset; its attribution exclusively to Qwen3-8B FullFT is unsupported. In-domain task score does not measure V7's generalization gap.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B FullFT, AdamW and Muon checkpoints
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AdamW or Muon and compared validation-NLL-selected checkpoints' Fisher trace and IFEval scores.

conditions.value: validation-NLL-selected checkpoint per optimizer and dataset

rows.measure: Muon trace was lower by a factor of 1.2 to 2.8 on every dataset; IFEval was higher on all four datasets, by a mean of 0.09.
rows.baseline: AdamW checkpoint on the same dataset.
rows.value: Muon: lower trace by factor 1.2 to 2.8; IFEval higher by mean 0.09.
rows.uncertainty: Task-judge difference was reported as a mean of 0.015 within the judge's resolution at 200 rows; one checkpoint per arm.
rows.note: Optimizer comparison measures task quality and IFEval, not the training–test gap.
rows.check: The numerical summary is supported, but AdamW versus hybrid Muon is not the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison specified by V4. Fisher trace and IFEval also do not measure V7.

relationships.condition: Customer-task language-model SFT at a fixed one-epoch, 5,000-example budget; tested LoRA batches 8–64 and FullFT batches 16 and 64.
relationships.reason: Based on text rather than existing rows: §2.3 explicitly reports lower validation NLL with smaller batches at the fixed epoch budget, consistent with V5 in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports lower validation negative log-likelihood with smaller batches after one epoch, but the comparisons remain unverified and establish no critical batch threshold.
